note: Product defaults (spec §8). Weights are tunable, not scientific constants. 1.1.0: every number the PresetEngine uses is now a machine-readable field (1.0.0 kept some of them only inside prose); added the per-region cap, the full tie-break order and the search-family declaration. See docs/preset-policy.md.
candidate_region_rule: every catalogue region of these layers that has a prepared series for at least one selected variable; basin4 sub-basins and hex cells are reachable by user selection but are not searched automatically (hex has no series). A region the user selected is the only candidate region, whatever its layer.
window_alignment: calendar years: Jan of start year to Dec of end year, anchored on the last complete common year and stepped backwards
candidate_period_rule: periods are derived from data availability only: the common period of the region is the intersection of the valid data of every selected variable whose approved product supports a trend on its record; candidate periods are that full common period plus every fixed calendar window of window_lengths_years that lies inside its complete calendar years. A period the user selected is the only candidate period. No slope, p-value or index value is read when candidates are declared.
min_variables_rule: a candidate (region, period) is analysed only when at least this share of the selected variables has an approved product that supports a trend for exactly that region and period; otherwise it is excluded before any computation and listed with the reason
missing_component_rule: a missing component scores 0 and is listed in missing_components; weights are not renormalised

effect.definition: abs(slope_per_decade) / sd of the fixed-baseline anomalies in the baseline period, squashed with x/(1+x)
effect.aggregation: role-weighted mean over the analysable variables that have a positive baseline sd; a variable without one is listed and left out; no such variable -> the component is missing

relevance.aggregation: role-weighted share of the selected variables that are analysable for the candidate

quality.definition: mean over analysable variables of coverage inside the window times (1 if inference applicable else descriptive_only_factor), reduced by fallback_or_caveat_penalty (not below 0) for a fallback product or a registered caveat

stability.definition: share of analysable variables whose first-half and second-half descriptive slopes have the same sign as the full-window slope; variables without both half slopes or with a zero slope are left out; none left -> the component is missing

aggregation: fixed weighted mean across variables, so more variables do not raise the score by count
significance_rule: statistical significance is not an input of the score; candidates are labelled has_significant / none_significant / undetermined_only from the preset-search family and can rank in any of the three states

search_family.definition: every hypothesis of every analysed candidate of one search batch: regions x periods x (variable anomaly trends + every metric of every selected indicator recipe + recorded-event metrics); BY-adjusted as ONE family; hypotheses without a valid p-value stay listed with the reason

max_presets_per_region_rule: applies to automatic presets only and only when the region is being recommended (the user left it blank); it keeps the returned list from being one region with many windows. It never removes a candidate from the search family.
